steps.title: A claim on trial
steps.idea: A hypothesis $H_0\colon a = a_0$ is put on trial against an alternative $H_1$. The evidence is one number computed from the sample, the statistic $U$. If $H_0$ is true, $U$ follows the standard normal law; if the true mean is $a$, the same law slides to $\delta$.

layers.intuition: The white curve is the law of $U$ in a world where $H_0$ is true, the cyan curve in the world where the mean is really $a$. A test cannot know which world it lives in; it only sees one value of $U$.
layers.definition: A statistical hypothesis is a statement about the law of the data. The null hypothesis $H_0$ is tested; the alternative $H_1$ is what we accept when $H_0$ is rejected. A test is a rule that maps every sample to a verdict.

steps.title: The critical region
steps.idea: Fix in advance the values of $U$ that are too unlikely under $H_0$: the critical region $\mathcal{K}$. If $U$ falls into it, $H_0$ is rejected. Its size under $H_0$ is the significance level $\alpha$.

layers.intuition: The coral sliver is the price of the rule: in a world where $H_0$ is true, that share of samples still lands in $\mathcal{K}$ and convicts an innocent hypothesis.
layers.details: For a right-sided $H_1\colon a > a_0$ the region is $U > u_{\mathrm{cr}}$ with $\Phi_0(u_{\mathrm{cr}}) = \dfrac{1 - 2\alpha}{2}$; for a two-sided $H_1$ it is $|U| > u_{\mathrm{cr}}$ with $\Phi_0(u_{\mathrm{cr}}) = \dfrac{1 - \alpha}{2}$, where $\Phi_0$ is the Laplace function.

steps.title: Errors of two kinds
steps.idea: A test rejects a true $H_0$ with probability $\alpha$ and keeps a false $H_0$ with probability $\beta$; the power is $1 - \beta$.

layers.intuition: Shrinking $\alpha$ moves the border right: fewer innocent convictions, but more of the cyan law stays outside $\mathcal{K}$ and $\beta$ grows. Only a larger $n$ lowers both, because it pulls the two laws apart.

steps.title: A thousand verdicts
steps.idea: Now draw samples from the world where the mean really is $a$. Each sample gets its verdict; green convicts the false $H_0$, violet lets it go. The share of convictions settles at the power.

steps.title: When $H_0$ is true
steps.idea: Switch the world: the samples now come from $H_0$ itself. The coral verdicts are type I errors, and their share settles at $\alpha$, whatever $n$ is.

steps.title: The power curve
steps.idea: The power depends on how far the truth is from $H_0$. At $a = a_0$ it equals $\alpha$; it climbs towards 1 as $a$ moves into $H_1$, and climbs faster for larger $n$.

layers.details: For the right-sided z-test $1 - \beta(a) = 1 - \Phi\!\left(u_{\mathrm{cr}} - \dfrac{(a - a_0)\sqrt{n}}{\sigma}\right)$. The dots are the share of rejections among 400 seeded samples at each $a$, drawn with common random numbers, so they rise with $a$ like the curve.

steps.title: Comparing variances
steps.idea: The ratio of two sample variances follows the Fisher–Snedecor $F$ law under $H_0$.
